Hello everyone,
For some other projects, I needed the hypothesis that ProbabilityMeasure.normalize is a measurable function. I didn't find such lemma on loogle (nor on the files but i might have missed it ?).
I've just finished the proof, and I was wondering if that were an useful PR to make ? To prove that it is measurable, I also proved that the mass function for finite measures is measurable, and a different 'version' of the lemma on scalar product with measures (smul_measure)
These are definitely useful lemmas that we should have. Aren't these functions even continuous?

I did not need that as assumptions for the proof, just that the probability measure is on a non empty measurable space

theorem measurable_normalize [Nonempty Ω] [MeasurableSpace Ω] :
  Measurable (MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.normalize)
  (β := ProbabilityMeasure Ω) :=
by /- ... -/

I was asking if the stronger result was true, because if it's true it's definitely worth having, and then deducing measurability from continuity. But in fact it's not, we can't have continuity at the zero measure. I guess it's true that it's continuous away from the zero measure, which implies measurability, right?

That's a good question... We are using normalize for the semantics of a small probabilistic programming language, where normalize is only used when the measure applied to Set.univ is not equal to zero...

Sébastien Gouëzel said :

I was asking if the stronger result was true, because if it's true it's definitely worth having, and then deducing measurability from continuity. But in fact it's not, we can't have continuity at the zero measure. I guess it's true that it's continuous away from the zero measure, which implies measurability, right?

In which topological space the continuity of FiniteMeasure.normalize is defined? It does not seems that Mathlib has an instance of TopologicalSpace for FiniteMeasure Ω nor ProbabilityMeasure Ω and I'm not sure if there is even one. Moreover, isn't docs#Continuous.measurable requires assumptions on the σ\sigmaσ-algebra of finite and probability measures that we don't have? I apologize if I miss something obvious here.
But they do indeed not apply at the generality of normalize.

There are two standard topologies on the space of probability measures, say: the topology of weak convergence, and the topology of total variation convergence. We have both in Mathlib, see docs#MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure.instTopologicalSpace and docs#MeasureTheory.LevyProkhorov.instPseudoMetricSpaceProbabilityMeasure (the former needs in addition a topological space structure on Omega). I was thinking you were looking at measurability for the Borel sigma-algebra generated by one of these two topologies, but if you're not I agree my comment doesn't make sense!
(Oops, my second pointer is nonsense, Levy-Prokhorov coincides with the topology of weak convergence in reasonable cases. I don't know if we have the topology for the total variation distance)

Sébastien Gouëzel said :

(Oops, my second pointer is nonsense, Levy-Prokhorov coincides with the topology of weak convergence in reasonable cases. I don't know if we have the topology for the total variation distance)

I'm pretty sure we don't have total variation distance (see #37730 by @Rémy Degenne). If anyone feels like working on it this should probably be defined from MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.variation.

Thanks a lot for the pointers! I should have thought of these convergences. And the fact that they require some structures on Ω\OmegaΩ explain why the inference system did not find them in the first place. I guess we could have a topology using the Wassertein distance as well, is it something that somebody is working on?
